2026 VTEM Survey Program

The VTEM Program was designed to improve the Company’s understanding of subsurface geology across four (4) of its British Columbia exploration Projects by mapping variations in electromagnetic and magnetic response.
Surveying was completed across:
Alturas Antimony Project
– West and East Blocks
Hurley Antimony Project
– West and East Blocks
Quarry Antimony Project
Lotto Tungsten Project

Geotech utilized its helicopter-borne VTEM time-domain electromagnetic and magnetic system. The resulting datasets significantly upgrade the resolution and quality of geophysical information on the Projects and provide key information regarding subsurface conductive features, geological contacts, structures, and magnetic patterns that can be evaluated for metal enrichment alongside the Company’s existing exploration datasets.
Convolutions Geoscience Corp. (“
Convolutions
”), led by Kyle Patterson, P.Geo., provided external quality-control review of the survey data during acquisition and is supporting the Company with geophysical interpretation and targeting.

Following receipt of the final processed datasets, Maxus intends to integrate the geophysical results with available geological mapping, historical exploration data, surface sampling, and other project-specific datasets to refine areas for follow-up exploration programs.
Preliminary Alturas West Interpretation
As announced by the Company on September 15, 2026,1 preliminary VTEM data from the Alturas West Project have already been incorporated into the Company’s exploration program.

First-pass interpretation and Maxwell plate modelling completed by Convolutions identified multiple fitted conductive responses distributed along a corridor spanning more than nine hundred (900) metres of the mapped Alps-Alturas shear zone, including responses beneath or adjacent to the historic Alps-Alturas mine workings (Please see Figure 1).

The modelling provided additional constraints on the potential location and geometry of conductive sources and was integrated with mapped geology, historical workings and structural measurements as part of the Company’s 2026 drill-targeting process.

The Company cautions that the fitted Maxwell plates represent simplified and non-unique models of possible conductive sources. The geological sources of the conductive responses have not yet been confirmed, and geophysical responses do not, on their own, establish the presence, grade, or continuity of mineralization.

Interpretation of the Alturas West survey will continue to be refined following receipt of the final processed survey dataset and integration with observations from the recently completed 2026 drill program.

Next Steps
Receipt of the final processed VTEM and magnetic datasets will allow the Company and Convolutions to advance Project-specific interpretation across the survey areas.

The Company intends to use these datasets as one component of its broader exploration targeting process, integrating geophysical responses with geological, structural, geochemical, and historical exploration information where available. Priority areas identified through this work may be considered for follow-up mapping, prospecting, sampling, additional geophysical interpretation, and/or drill-target evaluation, as appropriate for each Project.
Maxus expects to provide further updates as interpretation of the final datasets progresses.
Community Engagement

Maxus recognizes that meaningful engagement with First Nations and local communities is an important component of responsible mineral exploration. The Company remains committed to maintaining transparent communication, minimizing environmental disturbance, and building respectful long-term relationships as exploration activities progress.
